body-eating.question: What happens if you stop eating?

body-heart-attack.question: What actually causes a heart attack?
body-heart-attack.content: A heart attack usually happens when blood flow through a coronary artery is suddenly blocked, often by a clot forming where fatty plaque has damaged the artery wall. The heart muscle beyond the blockage loses oxygen and can be injured, so emergency care matters.

body-liver.question: Can you survive without your liver?

aging-whales.question: Why don't blue whales get cancer more often?
aging-whales.content: Large animals have many more cells, which might seem to create more chances for cancer, but cancer risk does not rise simply in proportion to body size. Whales appear to have evolved protective biology, though researchers are still studying the details and cannot say cancer never occurs.

aging-blood.question: Why do we have different blood types?
aging-blood.content: Blood types depend on inherited markers on red blood cells, including the ABO and Rh systems. These markers matter for safe transfusions because the immune system may attack incompatible blood cells; different types are normal genetic variation.
